chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Fadalah from Al-Husayn from Zayd al-Shahham and Ibn Abi Umayr from Abu Ayyub from Zayd al-Shahham said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'The opening [Takbirat al-Iftitah],' he said, 'One Takbir suffices for you.' I said, 'And the seven [Tasbiحات]?' He said, 'That is the excellence [Sunnah/additional virtue].'

key_terms.السَّبْعُ: The seven (referring to the seven Tasbiحات of glorification)
key_terms.اَلْاِفْتِتَاحُ: The opening Takbir (Takbirat al-Iftitah) at the start of prayer
key_terms.اَلْفَضْلُ: Excellence or additional virtue (Sunnah, not obligatory)

ai.seo_question: How many Takbirs and Tasbiحات are required in the opening of prayer according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* distinguishes between the obligatory minimum and the recommended excellence in prayer rituals, establishing that while a single Takbir suffices for the opening, reciting seven Tasbihs represents a meritorious addition (fadl) rather than a strict requirement. This distinction reflects the Shia juristic principle of differentiating between *wajib* (obligatory) and *mustahabb* (recommended) acts, allowing worshippers flexibility in adhering to the Sunnah of the Imams. The hadith underscores the importance of precision in ritual performance while encouraging voluntary acts of devotion to enhance spiritual presence.
